title: Bruschetta con Cannellini
subtitle: Toasted bread rubbed with garlic and topped with dressed white beans
excerpt: Bruschetta con cannellini is toasted sourdough rubbed with raw garlic and topped with white beans dressed in olive oil, lemon, rosemary, and flaked salt. The beans are creamy and mild; the garlic, oil, and rosemary make them taste alive. It is a ten-minute antipasto with nothing to hide behind.
sourceNotes: Bruschetta, toasted bread rubbed with garlic and oil, is a central Italian preparation documented throughout Tuscany and Umbria. The combination with white beans (fagioli) is a Tuscan classic that appears in Artusi, La scienza in cucina e l'arte di mangiar bene (1891), public domain, in various preparations. The specific bruschetta format is twentieth century.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Dress the beans up to 2 hours ahead. Toast the bread just before serving; it goes soggy quickly once topped.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian toasted or grilled bread rubbed with raw garlic and drizzled with extra-virgin olive oil. Pronounced broo-SKET-a, not broo-SHET-a. The name comes from the Italian verb bruscare, to roast over coals.

content.text: con cannellini has three components: good toasted bread, raw garlic rubbed over the surface while still hot, and white beans dressed simply with extra-virgin olive oil, lemon, rosemary, and salt. The quality of the olive oil matters here more than in almost any other dish, because it is applied generously and consumed without cooking. The bread should be sturdy enough to support the beans without collapsing.

Combine the drained {{cannellini-beans}} of cannellini beans in a bowl with {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} of olive oil, the juice of {{lemon}} half lemon, and the {{rosemary}} of chopped rosemary. Season with {{salt-flakes}} of flaked salt and {{black-pepper}} of pepper. Toss gently and taste. The beans should be well-dressed, not dry.

Toast the {{sourdough}} slices under a hot grill or on a griddle pan for 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden and with some char at the edges. While the toast is still hot, rub the cut side of a {{garlic}} clove over the surface of each slice. The toast's rough surface grates the garlic as you rub, depositing flavour evenly.
Spoon the dressed beans generously over each slice and serve immediately.

items.cause: The beans were dressed too far ahead, or the bread was too thinly sliced.
items.fix: Assemble and eat immediately. Dress the beans up to 2 hours ahead but spoon onto the toast only at the last moment. Thicker slices of bread hold up better.

items.symptom: The garlic flavour is too strong
items.cause: The clove was rubbed too many times over the surface, or the garlic was old and pungent.
items.fix: One or two passes over the warm toast surface is enough. The garlic should be noticeable but not dominant.

content.text: Bruschetta con fagioli is a staple of Tuscany, where white beans (borlotti, cannellini, or zolfini) are cooked in terracotta flasks by the fire in the classic preparation, then dressed with the local olive oil. The bruschetta format makes it an antipasto or a light lunch. The dish depends entirely on ingredient quality: good bread, good oil, and well-cooked beans.
